source_acquisition.search_note: The PDF Software paragraph on p.2 explicitly links the selected repository. GitHub metadata, README title/authors/conference, and the recursive main tree directly match the paper. The tree contains examples/linreg_dro.py, examples/portfolioopt_discrete.py, examples/portfolioopt_gaussian.py, examples/portfolioopt_gaussianmixture.py and utility code; these examples make generic single double-y-axis demo plots, while results are gitignored. No PDF-matching Figure 1–15 multi-panel generator, table generator, notebook, paper TeX/TikZ/PGF, final visual asset, or experiment registry was found. The examples are therefore recorded as related implementation paths in the Markdown search note, not as exact visual source files. No local corpus/visual_sources/icml-2026-a6577855483d directory or second public visual-source repository was found.

paper_style.palette_strategy: Local semantic tokens are reused across the paper: purple/orange for initial/final transport cost, blue/red for worst-case versus true or out-of-sample metrics, gray for no-penalty/neutral references, red transparent density contours for synthetic distributions, and a dark navy-to-coral sequential scale for Figure 15. Labels, line styles, panel position, and cell text provide partial redundancy, but color alone is not fully grayscale-safe.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: All 15 figures and 3 tables render as PDF vector paths/text at object scale; pdfimages reports only two tiny indexed image objects on p.36 (8×162 and 9×162), not full-size plot images. The audit rasterized all pages at 200 dpi for visual inspection.
paper_style.style_consistency: Letter-size single-column layout, black framed axes, light gray grids, Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern typography, and repeated blue/red and purple/orange tokens provide strong cross-object consistency. Local dual y axes, panel-local legends/colorbars, unreported uncertainty semantics, and the Figure 8 wording conflict are the main consistency breaks.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: Figure 1 defines the ambiguity-set geometry counterexample; Figure 2 moves from learned geometry to convergence and portfolio aggregate improvement; Figure 3 removes the coverage penalty; Figures 4–5 repeat the mechanism-to-effect path for absolute-loss regression. Appendix Tables 1–3 register hyperparameters and synthetic distributions/models, Figures 6–10 extend portfolio dimension and distribution family, Figures 11–13 switch to squared loss, and Figures 14–15 test penalty sensitivity and coverage violations.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Captions use plain Figure n:/Table n: labels without bold conclusion headers. Most figure captions identify panel order, colors, and before/after comparison, but error-bar/bootstrap and boxplot conventions are usually left to nearby prose. Figure 8 combines Gaussian-reference and true-discrete wording; the squared/absolute wording mismatch around Figure 12 is retained as PDF evidence.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Table 1 uses Parameter/Value; Table 2 repeats Dist./Mean/Covariance Matrix in two side-by-side blocks; Table 3 uses Model/Weight (w)/Variance (σ²). All are single-level headers without direction arrows, uncertainty columns, or result highlighting.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 is the method interface; Figure 2 and Figure 4 expose geometry and decision effects; Figure 3 directly ablates the coverage penalty in Eq. (13); Figures 5/7/12/13 aggregate objective effects; Figures 14/15 return to penalty robustness and constraint behavior. Algorithms 1–2 provide execution interfaces and Tables 1–3 provide the reproducibility registries.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: The main text calls Appendix A.2.2/A.3.1 for conic reformulations, E.1/E.2 for distribution/model generation, and F.2/F.3 for empirical-reference and squared-loss extensions. The appendix supplies stabilized Algorithm 2, registries, extra distribution families, loss variants, and sensitivity analysis while the main text retains the core geometry, results, and limitation.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Nimbus Roman No9 L and Computer Modern recur in captions, axes, tables, and equations; Figure 1 and all plot panels are vector, avoiding a raster-font discontinuity. Estimated internal plot sizes are approximately 6.5–10.5 pt, with captions near 9.963 pt.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Purple/orange cost and blue/red worst-case/true tokens recur from Figures 1–15, with gray for neutral/no-penalty controls. Figure 15 introduces a local sequential scale and Figure 4/6/11 use red density gradients; these local encodings are coherent but not a single global color scale.

most_reusable_patterns: Use Figure 1’s shared geometry counterexample to define the method interface before presenting results.
Pair single-instance geometry or trajectory with multi-instance sample-size objectives as in Figures 2 and 5.
Reuse mirrored before/after panels with a black attainable baseline for task and loss extensions (Figures 7–10 and 13).
Align performance boxplots and coverage heatmaps to one penalty-parameter grid (Figures 14–15).
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 is the shortest explanation of loss-aware ambiguity geometry.
Figure 2 is the most complete portfolio mechanism-to-outcome visual.
Figure 3 is the key coverage-penalty ablation.
Figures 4–5 close the regression geometry-to-error loop.
Figure 15 is the most directly auditable cell-level coverage object.
failure_patterns: Captions frequently omit error-bar/bootstrap interval, boxplot summary, and denominator definitions.
Figure 8 has an internal reference/true-distribution wording conflict; Figure 3’s zero/log-looking scale is unexplained.
Dual y axes and panel-local legends/colorbars raise comparison cost.
The linked public repository has generic plotting demos but no exact visual source for the PDF figures or tables.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses purple/orange geometry and blue/red worst-case/true tokens to move from a loss-aware transport-cost concept through portfolio and regression results to distribution, loss, and penalty extensions, while leaving uncertainty definitions and exact visual-source code incomplete.
